Hi Stephanie,

We're processing a Data Subject Request for one of our end users and need to understand what Redwood can and cannot remove from our account. The specific ask from our privacy team is: can you remove all user-identifiable usage records tied to the account while still providing us with invoices and a usage ledger sufficient for our internal audit and accounting? Our controller is concerned about preserving an auditable billing trail for FY26 while complying with the deletion request.

I've attached the DSR notice (Arc_DSR_request.pdf). Please let me know what Redwood's standard practice is here and whether we need an exception or special handling. The deadline from our side is next Friday, Dec 18.

Thanks,

Hi Kelly — thanks for sending this over and for the clear deadline. Quick summary up front: Redwood's default approach is to preserve accounting/billing records required for legal and tax obligations while removing or redacting user-identifiable fields from operational usage records where possible. There are a few trade-offs and a short workflow we recommend; I'm proposing that here so you can confirm.

Proposed approach (high-level):
- Preserve canonical invoices and the invoice numbering/amounts (we cannot void historic invoices required for accounting).
- Produce a sanitized usage export for your audit that includes aggregated usage metrics and per-invoice line items but no user-level identifiers (we'll redact user_id, session tokens, IPs, and any free-text prompts linked to the user).
- Maintain a restricted internal mapping (invoice -> internal usage IDs) for legal/audit queries for a limited retention window (access-controlled; not shared) if required by your auditor.

Can your finance team accept sanitized invoice exports in place of raw per-user usage logs? If yes, we'll deliver a redacted sample (Invoice_2026-11_redacted_sample.pdf) and a short plan. Rishi / Marissa — can you weigh in on the finance/accounting and compliance aspects below?

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen

Stephanie, Kelly — quick finance perspective. High level: we must preserve invoice records and amounts for statutory accounting and audit trails. In most jurisdictions Redwood is bound by finance record retention (commonly 6–7 years) and cannot delete historic invoices. That said, we can accommodate the DSR by producing redacted artifacts for you and keeping any mapping needed for internal investigations under strict controls.

Operational notes and the suggested workflow for Arc Therapeutics:
1) Invoice preservation: canonical invoice PDFs and the invoice ledger (invoice IDs, dates, amounts, taxes) will be retained verbatim.
2) Redacted usage export: we will generate a usage CSV per invoice with sensitive columns removed or hashed (user_id -> hashed_token, prompt_text removed, IPs removed). You will receive the CSV and a human-readable redacted PDF sample for validation.
3) Internal mapping hold: if your auditors require line-level reconcilability, we can place the internal mapping under a legal hold for a defined period (e.g., 90 days) with access restricted to Finance + Legal and encrypted with customer-specific KMS. This mapping would not be shared externally.
4) Accounting closure: we cannot retroactively alter invoice amounts or ledger entries. Any customer-led chargeback or credit must go through our normal billing adjustment process.

We should also confirm whether Arc needs the redacted exports to include per-customer aggregation (all users combined) or per-user hashed tokens so your audit can link usage to invoices. My preference is hashed tokens — it preserves reconcilability while removing PII.

I'll coordinate with Compliance on the exact retention windows and with Ops for export generation. Marissa — can you confirm whether 90 days internal mapping hold looks okay from a compliance standpoint?

—Rishi

Kelly — thanks for your patience. Based on Rishi's input and our standard compliance practice here's a short, actionable plan and timeline so your team can sign off: 

1) What we will provide (deliverables):
   • Canonical invoice PDFs (unchanged) for the requested period.
   • Redacted per-invoice CSV exports with user identifiers hashed and prompt_text removed.
   • One redacted PDF sample (Invoice_2026-11_redacted_sample.pdf) for validation.

2) Protection and limited hold:
   • If your auditor needs absolute line-level reconcilability, we will place the internal mapping under a 90-day restricted legal hold (access: Finance + Redwood Legal), encrypted with a customer-scoped key. That mapping will not be shared; it exists to support regulator/audit queries only.

3) Timeline:
   • Confirm acceptance of the redaction approach by end-of-day Thu, Dec 16.
   • We will deliver the sample redacted PDF within 48 hours of acceptance.
   • Full exports delivered within 5 business days after sample approval.

4) Next steps for you:
   • Reply to this thread to confirm: (A) redacted exports acceptable? (B) do you require the 90-day internal mapping hold for audit reconciling?

If that works I'll open the export job and loop in Ops to begin. We can also provide a short statement for your auditors describing the redaction steps we used.
